message.content:
**Answer:** One of the most celebrated and widely recognized sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin** (completed in 1889). --- ### Why “The Kiss” stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin (1840–1917) – a leading figure of modern sculpture. | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast). | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist; it captures intimate human emotion with naturalistic detail. | | **Impact** | • Became an icon of romantic love and sensuality.
• Influenced countless artists and became a staple in museums worldwide.
• Its dramatic pose and expressive faces set a new standard for figurative sculpture. | | **Legacy** | • Frequently reproduced in various materials (bronze, marble, plaster).
• Continues to be referenced in popular culture, literature, and film. | --- ### Other notable 19th‑century sculptures | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Significance | |-----------|--------|------|--------------| | **The Gates of Hell** | Auguste Rodin | 1880–1908 (unfinished) | A monumental work that showcases Rodin’s mastery of complex, layered composition. | | **The Thinker** | Auguste Rodin | 1902–1904 (early 20th) | Though technically from the early 20th century, it was conceived during Rodin’s late 19th‑century period and remains emblematic of modern sculpture. | | **The Venus de Milo** | (Ancient) | 150 BC | Not 19th century, but its rediscovery in 1820 sparked renewed interest in classical sculpture. | | **The Statue of Liberty** | Frédéric Baron Houdon (design) & Alexandre Gros (sculptor) | 1886 (dedication) | A monumental public sculpture symbolizing freedom; a landmark of 19th‑century engineering and art. | --- ### Bottom line While many masterpieces were produced throughout the 19th century, **Rodin’s “The Kiss”** is often cited as the most iconic and influential sculpture of that era, embodying the artistic innovations and emotional depth that defined the period.
